messages:
maya: Hey — doing a terraform apply for prod-ingress and it hangs on the state lock. Plan showed a diff on kubernetes_manifest.ingress.my-ingress that would replace because of an added annotation, but the apply never progresses. Error: 
```
Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

on backend.tf line 12, in resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tf_locks":
12: resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tf_locks" {}

Lock ID: 123e4567-89ab-cdef-0000-111122223333
```
maya: I think someone else might have a lingering lock, but `terraform force-unlock` is scary if someone's mid-apply. Any safe steps? @sam
sam: first step: check who holds the lock in DynamoDB. You can query the table with the lock id or just scan for the item. Usually it has a session info. `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-state-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "123e4567-89ab-cdef-0000-111122223333"}}'`
liam: if it's from an active apply you might see a timestamp and PID. If it's stale (older than ~10m) force-unlock. We had a case where CI left it for 2h.
maya: I ran the get-item and it's held by `ci-runner-42` with TTL 167... (about 35m ago). CI says its job finished 30m ago. So stale-ish.
olivia: before force-unlock, capture the current plan to a file: `terraform plan -refresh=true -out=stale.plan` so you can inspect what would change once unlocked. Also `terraform state list | grep kubernetes_manifest` to verify state entries.
maya: plan file shows replacement of `kubernetes_manifest.ingress.my-ingress` because cluster has extra annotation `ingress.kubernetes.io/managed-by: external` that's not in tf. We probably want to accept current cluster annotation and import/modify the state.
zane: you can import the current resource to state if TF doesn't manage it. Example: `terraform import module.app.kubernetes_manifest.ingress["my-ingress"] default/my-ingress`. Adjust the address to match your module path.
sam: right — workflow: 1) confirm lock is stale, 2) save plan, 3) `terraform force-unlock 123e4567-89ab-cdef-0000-111122223333`, 4) run `terraform refresh` or `terraform plan -refresh=true` to reconcile, 5) if you want tf to manage the annotation, update manifest in code and re-apply or import the resource if it wasn't in state.
maya: quick Q: will importing cause terraform to try to replace? Or will it just add state mapping?
liam: import just adds the resource to state; no changes applied. After import run `terraform plan` to see diffs — if there are drifting fields, plan will show them. To avoid replacement, you can `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` for that field temporarily.
infra-bot: CI check: recent pipeline #472 failed midway at 2026-02-25T13:12:09Z, same lock id. Marking run as aborted.
maya: ok I forced the unlock (it was stale). Then did an import for the ingress as `terraform import module.app.kubernetes_manifest.ingress["my-ingress"] default/my-ingress` — import succeeded.
maya: ran `terraform plan -refresh=true` — plan now shows only annotation change; will add lifecycle ignore_changes to avoid replacement and push a small PR. Anyone object?
olivia: :thumbsup: fine by me. Add a note in the PR explaining the ignore and follow up with a cleanup task to standardize the annotation source.
sam: good call. Also let's add a CI step to clear stale locks after X minutes or alert infra channel.
maya: thanks everyone — unlocked + imported + plan ok. I'll open PR to add ignore_changes and a follow-up ticket.
zane: resolved from my side. If you need me to apply once PR merged I can run apply and watch locks.
maya: appreciated, will ping you.
